app.tagline: Lore, basics and secrets of the world

eightBall.name: Magic 8 Ball
eightBall.shake: You shake the Magic 8 Ball. Something floats up through the dark water...

entries: Hold Shift to run. Running spends AP, the same meter your battle skills draw from. Walk or stand still to refill it.
Z acts on whatever tile you face. Facing a companion opens a quick chat, their Empathize sheet or the reserves.
Tab passes the lead to the next party member. Shift and Tab hands it back to the previous one.
Stuck in a wall? Hold Ctrl to walk straight through it while CTRL noclip is on in Options. It is on by default.
F9 quicksaves and F10 loads the latest quicksave. The game also autosaves every time you change map.
Every long list has a search strip. Press F or click the magnifier to open it.
The mouse never moves your character: dragging pans the camera, the wheel zooms the world map and hovering names things.
There are no random encounters. Every monster stands on the map with its level over its head.
A monster's level tag is a warning: white is a fair fight, yellow is tough, red is deadly.
A gold level tag marks a rarity: a creature that exists only once in your world. Meet it and it never appears again.
Fleeing always works, except against a boss, where it may take a few tries.
In each fight, a character at full health survives one blow that would have killed them. Someone already hurt does not.
The party holds 3 members. Anyone extra waits in the Reserves, and a 4th companion can walk along outside the fighting.
Money is euros. The only other currency is the arcade token.
The name tells you the cost: magic is written in CamelCase and spends MP, a plain worded skill usually spends AP.
INT drives the learned, technical and elemental schools: Arcanism, Pyromancy, Cryomancy, Electromancy, Idromancy, Aeromancy, Geomancy, MetaMagic, AstralMagic and Technomagical.
WIS drives the schools of faith, nature, death and fate: HolyMagic, Healing, Necromancy, ForbiddenMagic, VoidMagic, Augury, ChaosMagic, StatusMagic, Chronomancy and Convokation.
STR hits and carries, CON defends and carries, INT casts, WIS resists magic, DEX acts first and dodges, PSI is luck.
PSI is luck in every sense: critical hits, rare finds, darker grimoire pages and the odds of a bribe all lean on it.
Most weapons scale on STR, firearms on DEX and the heaviest on both. The equip screen highlights which stats a weapon uses.
Any class can wield any weapon. Skill with each kind is a proficiency of its own, and every battle won with it equipped teaches a little.
Each character carries 9 skills into a fight. Basic moves and skills lent by gear come free.
Some skills ask for a minimum stat. Only your own body and training count toward it, never your gear.
A skill lent by gear can be used even below its stat minimum, but it may fumble and waste its cost. The skill card says how risky it is.
Knowledge points belong to the whole party. Every new member adds KP the first time they join.
You earn KP by being curious: reading a book or studying a statue for the first time, browsing new web pages, scanning objects, dreaming.
In your own schools the roots of the skill tree are always open. Other schools open once you have a foothold, at a steeper price.
The deepest Esoteric and Forbidden branches of a skill tree wait until you are experienced enough.
Specializations are learned by doing. Whoever does the work learns the most, and the rest of the party picks up a little.
Points left over at character creation are banked. Spend them later to jump a specialization up a tier.
Every class has one signature passive that is always on, in and out of battle. Find it on the status sheet under Class Abilities.
Every class has a Hyper, a limit break that shows up once a character is badly hurt during a fight. It can be used once a day.
For the turn of its Hyper the user is untouchable. A Freelancer borrows someone else's.
Fuse Spells melts two abilities into one with the effects and costs of both. A failed roll loses the KP and forgets both parts.
In a spell fusion the dominant slot sets the shape of the result. Your INT helps the roll, and a perfect roll creates something exceptional.
Craft Spell builds an ability from parts: a core, an amplifier, a shape, riders and refinements. Roll it fills every row at random.
An enchanted weapon bursts its spell on every critical hit. Enchanted equipment triggers its spell when the wearer is struck hard.
An enchanted book casts its spell for free whenever it is read, but it may burn. A skilled Enchanting reader keeps it longer.
Hexorcize breaks magical gear down into KP. Richer, stronger and enchanted pieces give more.
A grimoire's offers are fixed the moment it is opened. Closing it or changing reader will not reroll them.
Write Skill Book and Write Grimorie copy what your party knows into a book, so others can learn it page by page.
An Expression Seed unlocks a character's Expression. The more a power is bound by limitations, the less it costs and the further it reaches.
Expression limitations can be strange: never on a chosen day, only by night, only against one kind of creature, only at a price in blood or gold.
Agility decides where the party's turns fall against the monsters', but your own members act in the marching order set under Turn Order.
A monster you ran from stays wounded while you remain on the map. Leave, and it heals and the corpses are gone.
Nearby monsters may join a fight. Something far above your level always fights alone.
Aim picks a body part for your next blow. Big parts are easier to hit, small ones harder, and a part already hurt is easier still.
Vital organs are hard to hit and only finish a monster once it is badly weakened.
Blunt blows break bones but never destroy a vital organ. Someone beaten down with blunt blows is left downed instead of dead.
Piercing damage slips past most defences, even Divine Shield and Magic Reflection.
Cutting, piercing and explosive blows can sever a limb. Take a hand and you take the weapon it held.
Wrestle costs nothing, needs no training and never takes a loadout slot. Most holds need a Grapple first.
Rip is a long shot in a wrestling match, but it can tear a limb clean off.
Talk to a monster before you hurt it: every wound sours its disposition toward you.
Insult and Throw a stone always land when talking to a monster. It will like you less afterwards.
Petrodemons cannot be talked to, shrug off Petro and fear fire. They pay out in crude oil.
A monster that can talk may spare you and walk away, if it likes you or thinks you too weak to bother with.
Nine elements run through every fight: Physical, Fire, Ice, Thunder, Water, Petro, Wind, Sacred and Cursed.
A Wet target fears thunder more than fire, and an Oily one is waiting for a spark.
Ice leaves a target Cold, and a cold target burns all the better. Freeze first, then set it alight.
A burn never goes out on its own. Wet targets and most reptiles shrug much of the fire off.
Thunder punishes Wet and Floating targets most. Machines, drones and armoured knights usually dread it.
Ghosts and most oozes shrug off physical blows. The Ethereal state does the same for you, while every element hurts far more.
Sacred is the bane of demons and the undead. Cursed hurts many humans and goblins, while robots and angels hold firm.
Wind lifts targets into Floating: thunder hurts them more, physical blows less, and Petro not at all.
Some creatures heal from the very element that should hurt them. The Bestiary tells the whole story.
The three Infusion spells always land on the whole party, and they act last in the round.
A magazine is never refilled between fights. Reload before the next one, or Attack turns into a Bash.
Gun-Fu lets you use Martial Arts with a gun or bow in hand, with a free shot after each one.
Some enemy ultimates must be dodged in a bullet hell: the more shots you take, the harder the blow lands.
Only one summon can be out at a time. It costs blood, MP, euros or stranger things every turn, and leaves when you cannot pay.
Some rites summon what you prepared: a creature you marked, the last thing you killed, even a companion you lost.
A summon always matches the strength of the fight it is called into.
A familiar belongs to whoever called it. The same character always meets the same familiar, and it grows with them.
What answers ConvokeFamiliar depends on your class: a Necromancer meets something dead, a Mechanic something built.
Mimic copies fade when the battle ends. Mutation is the exception, fusing strange creatures into your body for good.
A boss dies once for the whole world, in every savegame of it, and the kill goes into the Historical Archive.
In Strategic Battle, spears and whips reach further than swords, and bows and guns further still.
In Strategic Battle you cannot run with a monster right beside you. Step away first.
In Strategic Battle, townspeople who like you, or are simply brave, may take your side.
Running from any arena fight ends your streak, and the prizes grow with every win.
Every roaming monster has a temperament. A sentry watches one direction and can be crept around. An ambusher waits until you are close.
A lone pack animal keeps its distance and calls the others.
Monsters grow stronger as the years pass. A later starting date means a harsher world, with richer loot to match.
Every party member has six needs: Hunger, Sleep, Hygiene, Company, Fun and Bladder.
Time only moves when something happens: it creeps as you walk, stops when you stand still and leaps ahead when you sleep.
Running makes every need drain faster.
A meal is worth its calories, fat and protein. Its price says nothing about it.
Eat past full and the stomach empties faster. Gorge too far and Nausea follows.
Bitter cold and heavy heat both make you hungry sooner.
Let hunger run dry and the whole party loses health with every step until somebody eats.
Time awake only resets in a real bed or a cryogenic pod. Go days without and dreams turn hostile.
Company only drains for a lone traveller. Travelling together keeps it up, and a pet helps too.
Swimming leaves the whole party cleaner. Drinking sea water leaves everyone with Nausea.
A craving meter runs backwards: empty is content, full is withdrawal. Cravings ease while you sleep.
One dose rarely clears withdrawal.
Healing potions do nothing against disease. You need medicine, taken day after day.
A new illness stays nameless for a few days. Once named, a sick member takes the right medicine each morning by themselves.
Skip too many days of medicine and the cure starts over.
Illness wears you down but never kills. Beat one and you may be immune, though some always come back.
A hysteria is caught by witnessing it and spread by talking about it.
A clinic never fails. Field surgery is free, but a gamble, and bad weather makes it riskier.
A tougher constitution makes room for more augments. The right augment can slow, stop or even reverse a need.
Healing never regrows a severed limb. A clinic can fit a new one.
A badly hurt limb can choke the Ley Vein that runs through it.
Coffee and alcohol fill the bladder faster. A swim sets things right for the whole party.
A night's rest never ends in an accident, and on the open road the party stops by the roadside in time.
Short rests add up over time. Sleeping rough heals no wounds unless there is a Bedroll in the pack.
Waiting heals no HP, but slowly restores AP and MP.
Cryogenic sleep skips ahead to a day you choose, for 30 euros a day. People will have aged, married and died without you.
A night at camp also freshens hygiene and company around the fire, and somebody cooks for a hungry party.
Foraging in a vehicle only turns up litter from under the seats.
Only the backpack weighs anything. What you wear is free, and in a vehicle weight does not matter at all.
A world outlives any one adventure. Every party you play in it shares it and inherits what the others left behind.
An emptied chest stays empty in every savegame of that world.
Your other parties live on as characters on the map, going about their day. You can stop and talk with them.
Every world arrives with a century of alternate history behind it, from 1900 to 2001.
World settings are chosen once and can never be changed. To play differently, make another world.
In Goblin mode the Goblin Horde already rules most of Europe on the first day.
In an empty world the bank never opens, property is worth nothing and shelves are never restocked.
Severed magic means no spells, no MP and no brooms. Unbound magic means no guns, machines or modern gadgets.
In a world of chaos every level up teaches a random skill.
A world that starts in 2013 begins after the impact of 21 December 2012. There is no Earth, and the road leads to the Omega Tower.
The Atlas can step back through the years. Go back far enough and you may see the world before the Squishing.
Structure entrances are walked into, never pressed. Each one always leads to the same place.
The land above hints at what lies below: ice hides frozen caves, a graveyard hides catacombs.
Very rarely, an ordinary stairway down leads to a Holy Patron Bunker.
A hatch is found only on a patron's square. Below it lies a vault of rich loot.
A world map square with a ??? marker hides a branching adventure. Investigate it, but each one plays only once.
Some adventure paths open only to a leader of the right temperament.
Bologna is mapped street by street as one seamless city, and every building can be entered.
Homes lock only at night. Shops never do.
A tree falls to an axe in your pack, a rock to a war pick or a chipped pickaxe. Mining now and then turns up an ingot.
What you forage depends on the land: chanterelles in a forest, cloudberries on the tundra, dates in the desert, glowcaps underground.
Alien worlds offer nothing to forage, but their tentacle growths can be cut for meat.
From any elevator hall of the tower, the elevator takes you back to any floor you have already reached.
Below ground lies the lower tower, where the floor numbers run the other way.
You cannot save on the floors of the dungeon.
Touching anything alive in a dream moves you to another dream. Fall far enough and you wake up.
Dreams have no end. The longer you stay awake, the less the dream feels like yours.
In a dream, double tap jump while standing to take off.
Some maps hide stranger puzzles: warp pads, beams of light, crackable walls and clones that copy your moves.
Secret doors look like plain wall until you touch them.
With fog of war on, you see in the direction you face. Turning is how you look around.
Weather follows the season, the hour and the country. Crossing a border on the world map can bring a change of sky.
The screen tints with the temperature: blue in the cold, red in the heat.
Liminal walk on the world map takes you into the 3D world: the same Europe, built in cubes.
In the 3D world the deepest rock never gives. Ore seams drop straight into your bags as crafting materials.
In the 3D world a gun or bow digs from afar.
Fights in the 3D world happen where you stand, in real time. Your companions choose their own attacks, heals and revives.
Every vehicle you own can be driven across the 3D world. Asphalt, mud, sand and snow all handle differently, and the handbrake drifts.
The workshop can fit the camper to float and dive, or to fly. In the 3D world C dives and F takes off.
Any parked car can be stolen with a lockpick. Keys taken from a driver or a downed body open their car without a fight.
The bike needs no fuel and can be picked up and carried.
The flying broom needs no fuel, works indoors and lands on rooftops and bridges.
The inflatable boat has no storage. Keep it patched: a burst hull or lost oars leave you adrift.
The starship cannot use a roadside pump. It refuels only at an ordinary living star.
Fuel prices rise and fall with the world's oil market.
A fast travel countdown follows the real clock, so a journey left saved long enough may already be over.
Sleeping, waiting or foraging on the way makes a trip pass faster.
Short of money? Travel With No Ticket. A short hop is usually safe, a long trip rarely is.
With a bounty on your head, nobody will sell you a ticket. Taxis and your own vehicles never ask.
Only the driver grows in a vehicle's specialization. When they tire, someone better rested takes the wheel.
Riding a companion is faster than walking, and world map roads go by quicker in the saddle.
Party members and children can never be ridden.
Everyone you meet has a personality, traits, beliefs, money, a home, a job, a routine and a backstory rooted in your world's history.
Beasts hold no job, no money and no opinions. They answer in their own voice.
Opinion starts before a word is spoken: how well your traits and beliefs sit with theirs, how clean you both are, the way you look.
Opinion and attraction are two separate things. Talk and gifts shape opinion, courting shapes attraction.
Courting someone who does not want it is noticed. Keep at it and it becomes a crime.
Your outfit gives you four looks: Arcane, Substance, Stealth and Intimidation. People notice.
Robes and staves look arcane, daggers and light armour look stealthy, heavy armour and guns look intimidating.
Pickpockets steer clear of anyone who looks intimidating.
Each party member keeps their own standing with every faction and with every person.
The faction that holds the country sets your shop prices. If it truly despises you, its shops will not serve you.
Goodwill with a faction branch also counts with the hyperpower above it.
When two people wander close together they stop and talk, and every chat nudges their opinions of each other.
Lives go on even while you sleep: people move, marry, change jobs, retire and get convicted.
A topic heard by one character is known to the whole party. Options that need a topic stay hidden until then.
Your companions read the party diary too: the newest entries become what they talk about.
People far stronger than you will not follow you. Shopkeepers can be recruited too.
Abandoning a pet is a crime. Abandoning a child is far worse.
Each species reproduces its own way: live birth, eggs, seeds or splitting in two.
A creature built from two species takes its limbs, reach and weak points from both.
Elections follow each power's own custom, from ordinary ballots to papal conclaves and goblin moots where the loser may be eaten.
The people in office are real. They work in the capital and can be met.
Your party can found one political party per world. A new party starts with no supporters at all.
An election deposit is never returned, win or lose: 100 euros for a town, 2000 for a nation, 20000 for a hyperpower.
The Holy Vatican Empire picks its head in a conclave and takes no outsiders.
Every hyperpower holds a seat in the Assembly in Brussels. A character can join only once.
Resigning an Assembly seat costs far more standing than joining ever gave.
Meeting an army never starts a fight on its own. Talk to its leader, parley, attack or leave.
When two armies are already at war, you can join either side.
Every town tracks how prosperous, safe and happy it is. People out of work turn to crime, and the ripples reach the news.
A thriving town throws a festival. A miserable one is where epidemics strike cruellest.
A bounty never crosses a border. The other record waits for you to come back.
Heat fades with time, faster in the dark. While nobody is looking for you, an officer does not know your face.
Most deeds reach your record only if somebody saw them and chose to talk. Your own companions never talk.
A witness has to see you: close by, looking your way, with nothing in between.
A bribe is a dice check on the leader's PSI. A refused one is bribery, a crime of its own.
An incorruptible officer can never be bought, and the offer still counts against you.
Under canon law a Witch or a Gunmancer in the party is marked on sight, and esoteric magic is heresy, witnessed or not.
Horde law punishes theft and little else.
Self-reporting a crime on the N€police portal halves the fine.
Eris judges every trial, and in some moods she throws counsel out with no refund.
Defending yourself in court teaches the Law specialization. A hired advocate teaches you nothing.
Beat Eris in her own court and your bounty never grows again in that world.
A Police Officer in the party can sign off small charges as lawful acts every day. Canon law accepts no badge.
Streetwise training leaves less for the police to find, so the same deed costs a smaller bounty.
A coup de grace on a wanted person collects their bounty. On anyone else it is murder, if anyone sees.
First aid on a downed stranger gets them up at once, and they will remember the kindness.
A till nobody is minding is free for the taking, unless its keeper left it to join your party.
Stealing odds improve with DEX, Pickpocketing, darkness, a good Stealth look and an Invisible friend.
Every theft teaches the trade behind it, caught or not.
Eris feels differently about every party member, and may turn her attention to one of your companions.
The first date with Eris that ends well brings an Expression Seed.
Shop prices shift with the maker's share price on the stock market.
Company shares pay a dividend every day, more if you own most of the company. Oil and souls pay nothing.
A bank loan is due in 30 days. Past the due date the debt grows every day, even while you lie in cryogenic sleep.
Renting as a tenant costs 3% of the price on the first of every month. A missed payment gets you evicted.
A home bought in one savegame is off the market in every other savegame of that world.
A bench worker in a shop you own costs 10 euros an hour out of the till. Party members work for free.
A shop you own only sells while someone is on shift, and nobody restocks it but you.
A whole business never costs less than 5000 euros, and pays a profit every week.
Claiming the ground you stand on is free. Claiming someone else's is squatting, and costs a 25 euro trespassing charge.
Any world map square with three houses can become a town. Newcomers drift in and pay you rent.
Quest money and goods arrive by post. Visit a mailbox after handing a quest in.
A notice is written in the voice of whoever pinned it up, and some of them lie. Read between the lines.
Post inside one world is free. Write to your own party with a delay and it becomes a letter to your future self.
A worker leaves the party for the hours of a shift. Dressing the part brings better results.
On any d20 check a natural 20 always succeeds and a natural 1 always fails.
When the world offers a dice check, you can always walk away and nothing happens.
The Wish-Granting Orb costs 10,000 euros. A party with weak PSI sees the wishes as riddles, or worse.
Good news lifts a place's property prices and fills its shops for a while. Bad news does the opposite.
The real events of 2001 reach the news on their real dates.
A truly spectacular day of crime makes the front page.
Every recipe is written on the item itself.
Every forged piece is unique. Smelt melts a carried piece back into some of its materials.
Alchemistry reagents are paid when the bench starts, so cancelling refunds nothing.
The cooking pot combines 2 recovery items, and the order matters. Two of the same make a dish with a twist.
Carrying cookware improves every dish. You are warned if a meal would set off someone's allergy.
Raw meat and plant matter can be eaten raw, at a risk, or cooked into something better.
Brews ferment on the world clock, even while you are far away.
A greenhouse keeps plants growing all year. A Plant Mage in the party makes harvests far richer.
In spring a crowded hive may swarm, with half the colony flying off behind the old queen.
Dismantling furniture gives back most of its materials, along with anything stored inside.
Researching a node can raise stats for good, for your main characters in every savegame of the world.
The world remembers which leader made a discovery first.
Loot grows with the party's median level and the danger of the place. The deeper floors of the Omega Tower pay richest.
The biome decides what kind of loot turns up: a laboratory gives components and medicine, a crypt gives charms.
Online programs need a line. Underground, in caves or on alien worlds you are cut off, but the starship is always online.
Reading a web page for a while gives a little KP, once per page.
To boot, the hyperdeck needs a processor, memory, storage, a panel and a cell strong enough to power it all.
In the Chip Lab you draw your own logic and etch it onto a processor. More logic makes a faster chip, and a hungrier one.
Every song in the game is playing somewhere on the AM, FM or EM dial.
Watch a TV channel and you walk into its studio, where the cast turn to face you.
The HyperTamer pet lives in real time, even while the game is closed. It can die of neglect.
Lockpicking is a falling block puzzle. Fill a row from wall to wall and the lock turns.
A skeleton key opens any lock at once and is used up.
In Chaos chess, Black steals and transforms your pieces. Fill the Cheat Meter, then press Shift to break a few rules yourself.
Horse race odds are honest: a short price is a real favourite.
In the Monster Tournament the fights are real, and betting never affects the outcome.
The Minigames entry on the title menu plays any game for free, without touching a save.
Alone at a game table with nobody around, you play against your own subconscious.
The shooting range lends you the weapon, so you can try before you buy.
In the card game, once the board is full every monster fights its weakest neighbour.
Arcade cabinets cost 1 token a play, and unused tokens cash back in at the same rate.
In the book viewer, fling a page off the screen to tear it out.
Every game trains its own specialization. A game won lifts Fun more than a game lost.
Every planet has its own day and night, so the hour you land at depends on where you land.
On an alien world the danger is set by the planet alone. Read its biosignature before you land.
A world stripped of its resources stays stripped.
Black holes and dead stars cannot refuel you.
Somewhere in the sky a Dyson sphere waits.
Some worlds of the Milky Way are named after the game's patrons, and circle rare and exotic objects.
The night sky chart switches between the European and the Chinese sky with Tab: different figures in the same stars.
A coilgun hop between Greenwich and Apulia is free. Up to the starship costs 500 euros.
On the way up, a coilgun round crosses a belt of orbital debris, worse in storms and at night.
Every world starts with its own starship, always the same one for that world.
Under Permadeath, death deletes that party's saves. Its diary survives.
A full wipe under Permadeath leaves a gravestone. The world goes on.
Under Blood and Oil a bed restores only MP and AP, and losing a limb drops whatever it held.
Mods load in order, and the one at the bottom of the list wins.
The Auto Explorer plays for you while you stand still. A ruthless leader may steal what the party needs.
Two players can share almost every game in split screen. When they stand close, the two views merge into one.
Sandbox mode makes you Eris on the Disk of Discord, where crimes add no bounty.
The Hologram Check sends the party to a place you own without travelling. Take a door and the projection ends.
A Cultist learns nothing from the skill tree, only from books.
Gene splicing can change genetic traits, for 100 euros a point.
A Metamorphosis Potion opens every body and the face gallery. Leave without changing anything and it is given back.
Toiletries restore hygiene. Cosmetics raise your Substance look, and different ones stack.
A Feral or Ascetic soul hardly cares about hygiene. The Proud, the Noble and the Germaphobe care a great deal.
Holidays close offices, but shops stay open, and every holiday brings a gathering to town.
In a zombie world, runners see far and chase faster than you walk, and a screamer wakes every zombie nearby.
A zombie you kill stays dead. Flee instead and it is dazed for a moment.
When the Goblin Horde conquers a country, those who will not live goblin lives leave for camps by the border.
In a nation the Horde has ruled for a while, the goblins are ordinary citizens with names, jobs and homes.
Town traffic slows for people. Highway traffic does not.
The Raman scanner names what an object is made of. The first scan of each object teaches you something.
A unique piece's description lists every one of its past owners.
A thrown item stays where it lands, ready to be picked up, unless it falls somewhere that destroys it.
The Bestiary records a creature as soon as a fight begins, even if you run.
The Omega Tower looks like a skyscraper rising past the stratosphere. It is really a divine spear, hurled by Eris to kill Maat, goddess of justice.
Maat's body lies at the Omega Tower's lowest point, hundreds of kilometres under the crust, pinned in place by the tip of the spear.
Eris kills Maat on 21 December 2012. The spear flew 20 years into the past and through 92 dimensions, landing on 21 December 1992 in dimension 3: ours.
That paradox started the Squishing. Since 1992 fragments of other dimensions have been collapsing into ours, faster every year.
The Squishing works faster on higher numbered dimensions. The Green Fields, number 77, are already largely uninhabitable.
The Omega Tower pierces and connects all 92 dimensions. At its top waits the celestial throne of the deity who rules over every god.
The tower was built as an ark to carry humanity into another dimension. Driven into the Earth, it can no longer move, and now it is the glue holding the 92 dimensions apart.
The Omega Tower stayed sealed until 31 December 1999, when its door opened by itself as 2 billion people died in a single night during Y2K.
Inside, the Omega Tower is chaos: department stores beside underground jungles, reactors the size of a town, corridors full of camping tents.
The Archive Foundation was the first to explore the Omega Tower, and it keeps the peace there. Every faction treats the tower as neutral ground.
For millennia Eris was a C-list deity. Then, in the '90s, she fell madly in love with Bubba, a Neapolitan-Texan mechanic.
Eris and Bubba robbed banks along Route 666, which links the three Americas, using her power over probability to open any safe at once.
Their romance ended in December 1992, when the Eris of 2012 killed Maat retroactively and the Eris of 1992 had to take up her path to the throne again.
With Maat dead, Eris also runs the courts of every dimension. She has no talent for it, so she judges chaotically and arbitrarily.
Bubba still loves Eris and feels nothing for Em. Eris is jealous of Em anyway, and bends cosmic law and probability to make her life hell.
Eris holds billions of trials at once. For the worst cases she sends judicial ghosts that move in a straight line until they reach their target.
The Father aspect of YHWH died on 1 January 2001 during the Ritual of Solomon. Eris sat on the empty throne, and no god dared tell her no.
The Ritual of Solomon turned 92% of Em's memories into the Spear of Memory, the weapon that killed the Father aspect of YHWH.
Em was born in 1984 in Wimbledon, Britannia. She woke alone on the Ritual Island on 1 January 2001, with no past and enormous power.
Em lost 92% of her memories in the ritual, and for reasons nobody knows her magical potential grew exponentially.
Bubba is a mechanic from Westford, Texas. He is going to Beagle for the most down to earth reason there is: to sign the divorce papers.
Bubba once won a card game against Zephyr, the trickster god. The prize was a compass that points at the crossroads of fate.
Bubba built the first liminal engine in 1996. By 2001 it powers almost every form of public transport, which made him filthy rich.
The liminal engine compresses the road ahead and crosses Europe in minutes. It slips between dimensions, so the Rule of 80 has no hold on it.
A liminal engine's one weakness is a time bubble: run it close to one and the vehicle can come apart around its crew. Liminal routes keep well clear.
The Rule of 80: anything moving faster than 80 km/h is pulled toward the nearest time loop bubble, and the faster it goes the sooner it is taken.
Inside a time loop bubble every day resets. Entering costs nothing at any speed, but the only way out is to move outward faster than 80 km/h.
Inside a time bubble you can only die for good at over 80 km/h, or when struck by something going that fast. Everything else resets with the day.
No phone, spell or mind can reach across a time bubble's edge. Carrier pigeons with USB sticks carry the post, since a tailwind pushes them past 80 km/h.
On a road the Rule of 80 works through the asphalt: above 80 km/h the road leans toward the nearest bubble, and a driver who lets go of the wheel is steered into one.
The Trucker's Society carries goods, news and people between communities stuck in different time bubbles, and never sets out without an old Anoki phone.
Fantablack, scraped off the Omega Tower, makes anything painted with it immune to time bubbles. Bullets coated in it kill even inside a loop.
The inside of every vehicle with a liminal engine is coated in Fantablack.
Euro banknotes carry Fantablack in their security strip. With his name printed on billions of them, Mario Draghi ascended as a god of the market.
A god lives as long as people believe in them. To destroy Mario Draghi you would have to burn every banknote that bears his name.
A god who dies of oblivion turns to stone and falls into the White Desert. A murdered god stays anchored to reality and rots, still conscious.
The body of the Father aspect of YHWH orbits the Earth. Pieces of it that fall grant part of his power, even to people who cannot use magic.
Sacred magic dies with its god: most of the Vatican's sacred spells have been almost useless since 1 January 2001.
Every spell must be written and spoken in CamelCase. Split the words and the universe takes it for a transcendental, a formula of the gods, and sends you the bill.
A badly written spell in a grimoire infects the other words with copies of itself. Left unburned, it eats whatever sits beside it.
Magic flows along leylines, invisible rivers that well up from oil deposits. Close to one, spells hit harder but are harder to control.
Casting carelessly on a leyline can break it, and where a leyline is broken even simple spells barely work. Divine spells are the exception.
Ritual magic costs no MP. Sympathetic magic compresses a ritual into seconds for MP. Metamagic swaps gestures and words for pure imagination.
Petrodemons are sentient oil, almost indestructible beside a leyline. Some believe the dinosaurs were natural mages whose power stayed bound in the oil.
To kill a petrodemon you must break its leyline first. Most hyperpowers would rather sign contracts with them, since they can redirect leylines.
Enrico Mattei is said to have found a ritual to bind petrodemons in a Libyan tomb. Soon after he tried it, his plane went down in 1962.
King Solomon founded the Mages' Guild in 950 BC. It stayed secret until Margaret Thatcher showed magic to the world during the Falklands War.
Thatcher's Okeanus, the ultimate water spell, devoured the Argentine fleet on live television and started an arcane arms race.
Aleister Crowley refounded the Mages' Guild in the early 1900s as an order of chivalry, which is why its leaders are called Sir and Lady.
In 2001 the Guild's three pillars are Crowley for the past, Thatcher for the present and Shoko Asahara for the future. A pillar does not age while in office.
A pillar usually serves 50 years, but Crowley refuses to step down, and nobody can force him: he knows spells the gods do not.
One of the Mages' Guild's duties is to find and kill whoever Magamui is controlling. Magamui needs time to take a new host.
Magamui is an alien larva a quarter the size of the Moon, clinging to the Earth's core. It dug the great caves and the Serpentine Road.
The Inverted Citadel surrounds the Earth's core like a shell, with the core as its sun. Look up and you see other districts overhead.
The Inverted Citadel was built by a civilisation that lived between the dinosaurs and mankind and vanished without a trace. It is now the goblins' capital.
In May 1970 the Soviets dug too deep with the Kola Superdeep Borehole. The goblins climbed up the shaft and began their invasion of the surface.
Naguka goblins are human deep down and can have children with humans. A goblin and human hybrid is called an orc.
Harm one Naguka and the whole species turns on you: they share the Goblin collective unconscious.
Conquering Scandinavia, the goblins discovered Norwegian black metal. They now worship the band Junehem as gods and wear corpse paint into battle.
Junehem lead the goblin hordes through the collective unconscious. They cannot die while a single goblin still believes in them.
Hieronymus survived being stabbed by his bandmate Count Grissnack and became one of the strongest psionics alive. Nobody knows where he went.
The Verden are true goblins from dimension 77. They lay eggs and split in two, and a severed Verden limb planted in the ground grows a new Verden.
The Verden once had utopian technology. Thousands of years ago they threw all of it into their sun and took up farming and magic.
The Verden can read the Goblin collective unconscious through magic, but only read: they cannot plant anything new in it.
The Holy Vatican Empire is the only hyperpower with official ties to the goblins. Its missionaries hope to turn them into an army.
The Holy Vatican Empire rules Italy, Spain, Poland and East Germany. Only sacred magic and technomagic are allowed there.
Arcane mages caught in the Holy Vatican Empire are burned at the stake, or drafted into the Umbra Excidii to hunt other mages.
Pope Peter II, born Joseph Ratzinger, took the throne after John Paul II died following the attack of 13 May 1981.
Since the Father aspect of God died, Vatican City floats 800 metres above Rome on liminal engines, guarded by Gauss cannons.
America never won its independence. It is split into the Republic of Cascadia, the Independent States of the Midwest and the Atlantic Protectorate under Britannia.
Bill Clinton is president of the Independent States of the Midwest.
On 11 September 2001 a Thatcherite cell set off three theonuclear devices in New York. They spare buildings and disintegrate souls, leaving empty bodies behind.
The Ritual of Solomon can rewrite the source code of magic: make it easy for everyone, limit it to a few, or switch it off entirely.
Among the relics spent in the last Ritual of Solomon were the Iron Crown, the Spear of Longinus, the sword Tyrfing and clay from the Golem of Prague.
A mini Ritual of Solomon changes magic around you with one artifact instead of seven, but the effect fades and the caster risks death or memory loss.
During Y2K the ENVISAT satellite lost control and set off a chain of collisions. Within a year the debris made leaving the atmosphere suicidal.
The European space agency, led by Margherita Hack, launches rockets made almost entirely of armour, built to be shredded on the way up.
Launches from the Greenwich and Taranto spaceports are free for volunteers, because more than 90% of them end in disaster.
Canadafrica: in a single day all of Mexico and South America reshaped to look like Africa from space. The cities and people stayed exactly as they were.
Lava has been almost harmless since the Squishing: it drains your MP instead of burning you. Lava conjured by magic still burns.
Thought transmitted diseases pass from mind to mind. A mental dam of tinfoil around the head stops them.
Anoki phones were the first technology rebuilt with magic. They talk through the leylines, and well tuned they reach the afterlife or the gods.
The Hypercapitalist Collective spent so long above 80 km/h that their bodies resist the loop even standing still. They sell escapes from it.
The Hypercapitalist Collective controls the only clean water. Everything else is cut with LSD.
The Archive Foundation wants every scrap of information made public. Its checkpoints may stop you to publish the messages on your phone.
Nobody has ever seen an Esoteric Heavy Industries factory or worker. Its goods simply appear in the warehouse when nobody is looking.
Esoteric Heavy Industries goods ignore the time loop: move them below 80 km/h and they stay as they are.
The God of Asphalt created the first road and was the first victim of a road accident, at the hands of a superior god.
Every road in every world is part of the Encompassing Road. A well calibrated liminal engine can take a highway exit into another place, time or dimension.
The Scraps of Creation are pocket worlds the gods once used to test their powers. Since 1992 some of them have fallen into our world.
The Dargos come from Titania, an acid ocean world in Andromeda. They stand three metres tall, run hot and greet each other with pranks.
Crowley's wards around the Earth stop the Tourists' ships, and have never stopped a Dargos one.
In 1978 the night guard Pier Fortunato Zanfretta met the Dargos above Genoa. Eleven more visits followed, until 1981.
The Zanfretta Sphere is the only object the Dargos left behind, and the one subject the Dargos Embassy will not joke about.
Titania circles a black hole the Dargos call the neighbour. They say it is slowly pulling them in, which may or may not be part of the joke.
Eris starts out at -92 toward Em and +92 toward Bubba.
One stranger in five blames Em for the death of their god.
Illness spreads inside the party when you open the menu: each opening rolls once to see whether someone caught something from a companion.
Someone still incubating an illness cannot pass it on. They are most contagious at its peak, and only mildly before and after.
Some blood-borne viruses have a window period of months: you carry and spread them long before anyone can name them.
At a doctor's, each illness is diagnosed and paid for separately. Treatment can only start once an illness has a name.
The party takes its medicine by itself at 8 in the morning, one dose per illness per day. A dose taken by hand at 2 a.m. counts for that day.
Medicine for a lifelong illness only holds it down one day at a time. It never adds up to a cure.
A dose taken that day lowers the chance of that morning's symptoms and cuts about two thirds of the illness's HP loss.
An untreated illness slowly gets worse, until its penalties and need drain are double what they were at the start.
Untreated mange turns into MRSA after 24 days. An untreated sigil blight becomes ley rot in just 20.
Hepatitis B turns into cirrhosis after 25 years, even under treatment.
Mad cow disease can hide in a body for about 3,000 days before a single symptom shows.
Rabies does not spread by ordinary contact, but a leader who carries it can still pass it on by biting.
Fungal, parasitic, deficiency, mental, chronic and autoimmune illnesses leave no immunity behind. You can catch them again.
A member who beat an illness does not catch it again just by staying in a town where it rages.
Every world starts with three outbreaks already running: a mass hysteria, an ordinary illness and a rare, deadly one.
While you carry a hysteria, your need for company drains more slowly.
Start an epidemic on purpose and the news reports it as bioterrorism until it burns out.
Towns reached late by an epidemic already have quarantines and border checks, and suffer less than the first ones hit.
An NPC who catches a sexual illness that their partner picked up elsewhere finds out about the cheating, and the couple breaks up.
Unwashed people, children and anyone over 65 catch illnesses more easily.
In a world without magic nobody catches a curse. In a world of pure magic nobody catches a cold.
Pollen allergies flare only outdoors in spring and summer, in dry weather. Rain, storms and snow wash the pollen away.
An antihistamine blocks mild and moderate allergies. A severe one still breaks out, but only as hives.
Rh-null golden blood can be given to almost anyone, but its carrier can only receive Rh-null or Synthetic Delta blood.
Synthetic Delta blood suits every blood type, even blue hemocyanin and green chlorocruorin blood.
A plant-type character stays pregnant for good: each seed it makes starts the next one growing.
Mitosis takes a single day. The clone takes the original's name with a number, and joins the party if a slot is free.
A growing vat raises a creature in a quarter of its species' usual pregnancy.
A vital organ only becomes lethal once its owner drops below a quarter of their HP, monster or party member alike.
Party members lose limbs only to cutting or piercing blows. Monsters can lose them to explosions too.
A surgeon can graft any hand or foot onto any bare limb, so a foot can go on an arm. Grafted wings teach the Fly skill.
Crossing two species that both have arms makes a four-armed creature, unless the two share the same body plan.
A body holds 4 augments, plus 1 for every point of Constitution bonus. Genital implants do not count toward the limit.
A Somnologic Regulator stops the sleep need from draining at all. A Self-Cleaning Dermis makes hygiene rise as you walk.
Field surgery goes better in snow, because the cold slows bleeding. It goes worse in rain and worse still in a storm.
Hunger is one meter for the whole party: feed one member and everyone eats. A big feast can push all of you into overeating.
Eating anything when hunger is at zero brings HP back to full.
Hunger drains faster below 12°C or above 26°C, and cold costs more: at -10°C it drains nearly twice as fast.
A pet counts as half a companion toward the party's need for company.
After more than a day without real sleep the mind slips into Confusion or Rage. Stay up longer and you may fall asleep on your feet.
Being put to Sleep in battle rests your sleep need, and being soaked by a water spell counts as a wash.
Cryo pods refuse to run in December 2012. Any other time, a stay can last up to ten years.
Earth has three moons on Fridays. A ship parked at one of the extra moons is moved back to Earth orbit when Friday ends.
A losing spin soothes a gambling craving as well as a win, and one evening at the casino eases it for every gambler in the party.
Giving an NPC their fix makes the habit grow faster. Talking them round halves how fast it grows.
Travel with a Nurse and every illness is named on the day it is caught, so treatment can start at once.
Children go to school only on weekdays, and only if their town has a school. Otherwise they spend the morning at home.
An NPC caught shoplifting gets a record and a bounty of their own, and their faction loses reputation.
Nobody dies of age or illness on the map you are standing on. Their death waits until you are somewhere else.
When someone dies, their shares go to their relatives and an orphan is taken in by kin. A dead office holder is replaced.
The litter in a Horde town vanishes the moment the Horde loses that country.
On the highway walkers keep to the verge and cyclists to the shoulder, while broom riders fly over the median, where nothing can run them down.
A traveller who owns a car is never seen walking: they drive one of the cars on the road.
In a zombie world, who turned is fixed by the world seed: the same street holds the same dead in every save.
When a monster walks into town, fighters attack it if it is at most two levels above them and flee anything stronger. Children always run.
Someone knocked down in a brawl gets back up 6 to 12 hours later.
A badly hurt NPC goes to a clinic or pharmacy in town and buys medicine, and heals faster for it.
Only a manual save records where your other parties stand in the world. Autosaves and quicksaves do not.
Pregnancy depends on the species: a Naguka clutch is laid within weeks, while a Verden one takes over a year.
After a breakup, whoever is not on the lease moves out. With no room elsewhere in town, they may leave or end up on the street.
A couple living in two different towns keeps a home in each.
A child who turns eighteen keeps the beliefs they were raised with until their own life changes them.
Travelling NPCs weigh fares against what their time is worth: the poor walk, the rich are driven, and those who cannot pay stay home.
Sometimes a visit turns into a new life, and the traveller settles for good in the town they went to.
When the Horde conquers a country, its people flee one household at a time over one to three months. About one human in ten stays.
Refugees who find nowhere to go within three months stay put and make what life they can under the Horde.
Adventuring bands in the Omega Tower are drafted from real townsfolk. Ministers are never drafted, and now and then someone does not come home.
On an airless world, crew from Earth wear an EVA suit, while aliens breathe unaided and keep their own faces.
An adopted pet keeps ageing, but the background simulation never kills it.
Chatting slowly pulls an NPC toward the speaker's beliefs, more so with charisma, at most once per game hour. Someone who dislikes the speaker cannot be swayed.
NPCs take sick leave only once they show symptoms, and stay home 2 to 10 days.
A new parent who gave birth takes about five months of leave. Their partner takes one to three.
Being served at a counter earns the worker a small tip, and counts as a brief exposure to disease.
Losing a job halves an NPC's odds of owning a car, and an NPC who loses their car keys loses the car.
NPCs who lose a limb get a prosthetic weeks or months later, sooner if they are rich. Technophobes never take implants.
A town in an economic bust sees 1.6 times more divorces, and a festival makes people 1.4 times likelier to start dating.
An NPC only knows the deeds they saw, but arson and bodies shake a town even unseen. Kindness repairs a town more slowly than cruelty harms it.
A new recruit who takes a party slot does not inherit how the town felt about whoever held it before.
A demisexual or demiromantic NPC is hard to court until they already like you a lot. A sapioromantic one falls for intelligence over looks.
Friends teach their skills for free, neutral NPCs charge for it, and those who dislike you refuse. Party members teach each other for free.
Crimes committed at night raise 40% less heat.
A witness who likes the party may look the other way. The victim always reports you, however friendly they were.
A shopkeeper who catches you stealing never sells to your party again, even after the bounty is paid, and their shelves leave your steal list for good.
Inside the Holy Vatican Empire a manhunt takes three times as long to blow over.
Running from the fight with Eris always works: she heals you, puts back any limbs she took, and fines you.
In the first phase of the fight with Eris, nobody in the party can die.
About one townsperson in twenty is a creature, against roughly one in six out in the wild.
Only the first three party members get their class passives. A fourth companion's passive does nothing.
A Samurai's first action in every battle deals double damage and cannot miss.
Berserkers hit up to 40% harder as their HP drops, but all healing they receive is halved.
A Barbarian never takes more than 150% damage from an element they are weak to.
Firefighters take no damage at all from fire.
An Illusionist starts every battle with two mirror images, and each one cancels a damaging hit.
The Wretch lands more critical hits and dodges more the less money the party carries. The bonus is gone at 50 euros.
Cultists deal 15% more damage and take 10% less between 8 PM and 6 AM.
A Cultist copies spells straight out of books, past most of the level, stat and MP limits other readers face.
An Elementalist tunes in to the weather when a battle starts: rain boosts Water, storms Thunder, snow Ice and clear skies Fire.
A Spellblade's attacks take the element of the last spell they cast, with the full weakness bonus if it fits.
A Battlemage short on MP can still cast, paying the rest in AP.
Once per battle, a Demigod who takes a killing blow stays standing at 30% HP.
Each Knight above 25% HP soaks 15% of the damage aimed at the rest of the party, up to 45% with several Knights.
A Guardian's ward covers the whole party, weakens as the Guardian loses HP, and never blocks more than half a hit.
A Convoker stuns any enemy struck by three normal attacks in a row, and everything the party summons arrives 30% tougher and 20% stronger.
A Boxer gains a combo stack each time they dodge or are missed, up to five, all spent on the next action.
A Psyker cannot be confused, frightened or charmed.
With a Scout in the party you strike first far more often, and are ambushed a fifth as often.
Enemies pick a Mimic as their target only about a third as often as anyone else.
A Meteoarcanist regenerates extra MP and AP in rain, storms or snow.
An Archmage gets twice the KP out of every book.
A Lumberjack gets ten times the salvage from a tree. A Hunter-Gatherer doubles the salvage from anything.
A Police Officer can write off up to 50 euros of the party's charges each day for every level they have.
Every Mercenary in the party cuts the army's weekly wage bill by 5%.
A Gunmancer loads spells into the gun: a single target spell spends a bullet, and every reload gives back a fifth of their max MP.
Execute Hypers deal ten times their damage to an enemy that is badly hurt. The Rogue's kicks in below 35% of the target's HP.
The CEO, Mercenary and Shopkeeper Hypers hit harder the more money you carry, and spend none of it.
A Mimic has a 20% chance to learn for good any enemy skill that hits them, and picks up a random skill with every level.
A skill cast below its stat requirement may fizzle. Each missing point raises the chance, up to 75%, and the cost is spent either way.
Augments and grafted body parts count toward a skill's stat requirement. Gear, buffs and states do not.
A Wet target struck by Thunder is paralysed, and one struck by Ice has an even chance to freeze solid.
Frozen and Brittle enemies shatter under physical blows, taking 50% and 60% bonus damage. Fire thaws them out.
Fire on an Oily target spreads to every oiled neighbour. A Volatile target hit by fire explodes for double damage.
Elemental reactions only go off from skills made to trigger them. A plain weapon swing never sets one off.
A knocked out member gets back up at 1 HP after an hour of game time, unless you play a permadeath difficulty.
Roaming monsters grow 5 levels stronger for every year of game time. From 2012 nothing below level 80 is left.
How dangerous the land is depends on the straight line distance from where you started the game. Moving your sleeping spot does not change it.
Talk odds are the enemy's mood plus 5% for every PSI step you have over it, always between 10% and 95%.
Below a mood of 80, recruiting an enemy succeeds at a quarter of your talk chance. Asking it along as a pet adds 15% instead.
A monster more than 3 levels above the party's median level will never join you, so one veteran cannot recruit for a party of beginners.
Bosses never agree to surrender.
An aimed blow that misses its part hits nothing. Head hits concuss, eye hits blind, arm hits disarm, and leg or wing hits hobble.
A summon's d20 roll decides what it brings: a natural 1 brings only its basic attack, a natural 20 every skill it knows.
The same d20 sets how long a summon stays outside battle: one minute on a natural 1, eight game hours on a natural 20.
The Elder Entity is the one summon that ignores the strength of the fight. It drains its summoner dry in about three turns.
A Witch's familiar is a bat, a Necromancer's a skeleton, and a CEO's or Shopkeeper's a treasure chest mimic.
In map battles a diagonal step counts as one square, so a monster diagonally beside you is in sword reach.
In map battles attacks from the side hit 10% more often, and from behind 25% more often.
Cowards and pacifists never take your side in a map battle.
In the Boss Rush your party is set to each boss's own level before the fight.
In a bullet hell dodge, avoiding every shot still lets a quarter of the blow through. Ten hits or more make it land 50% harder.
An empty gun becomes a club, dealing 40% of its damage.
A six round burst hits about 2.4 times as hard as one shot.
A second weapon held without dual wield training cuts both weapons to 65% of their strength.
Samurai are the only class with a mouth slot on top of their hands: room for a third blade between the teeth.
A body with no hands holds its weapon in its mouth, and that slot takes anything, even a two handed weapon or a shield.
Past two weapons, your weapon stats become the median of everything you hold, and two random weapons swing each turn.
An untrained weapon works at a third of its strength. A Master gets 125% out of it.
Psychic skills draw on PSI, while firearms and Roguery draw on DEX.
Pain Transmutation ignores stats: it hits harder the more HP its caster is missing.
A fused spell is named from the first four letters of each of its parent spells.
Enchanted armour fires only on the first critical hit its wearer takes each battle.
An enchanted book starts with nearly an even chance of burning at each reading, less with Enchanting skill and knowledge of its school.
Enchanted gear gives 50% more KP when hexorcized. Gear you are wearing cannot be hexorcized.
A character who never uses an Expression Seed awakens one anyway: at level 15 in a magical class, or at level 25 otherwise.
Each limitation on an Expression makes it cheaper and lowers its stat requirements, but adds no raw power.
The party's median PSI raises the chance of a Forbidden page in a grimoire, up to 35%.
Throwing a disease vial at someone infects them. If anyone sees it, it counts as bioterrorism.
One SOUL starts at 666.66 euros on the stock market, and its price always drifts back toward that number.
Occult companies pay the fattest dividends on the exchange, 6% a year.
Dividends keep coming while you are away, but one payout never covers more than 30 days.
In a zombie world every stock trades at roughly a third of its fair value.
In a world of chaos every shop price is rolled from a quarter to four times normal. Free things stay free.
Loan interest and penalties stop growing at three times what you borrowed, and Accounting talks the penalties down.
In an empty world the bank never opens, and your debts freeze where they stood.
Any staffed business can be bought, even one inside the Omega Tower.
A benched party member can take a shift at a business you own, covering for the regular worker.
News can push a property down to a quarter of its value or up to four times it, never further.
Inn rooms are shared across every save of a world: a room booked by another of your parties stays taken that night.
Bashing in a locked inn door gets you a free night in the room, and a breaking and entering charge with it.
In an empty world locked rooms get kicked open and never lock again.
Stockbusters gives up to 40% off for a thousand of something, and parcels that land while the game is closed still reach you.
About one vending machine in ten sells nothing but weird items, and every other machine hides at least one oddity.
Each day any item has a 12% chance to be sold out at a given shop.
Sit at a restaurant table and you can order from the counter without getting up.
Stealing always works in an empty world, and at an unstaffed counter in a zombie world.
Night helps stealing outdoors. Indoors only a dark room counts, but caves, crypts, sewers and floors underground always do.
Mail to another world is priced in oil and souls together, and grows with the distance between the two dimensions.
Alchemy cannot fail if you meet every skill requirement of the recipe, and every two tiers above it add a flask, up to four.
A dish cooked from two items takes the first word of one and the last word of the other.
Raw meat and raw plant matter refuse to be cooked together, though each one cooks with itself.
Rain makes crops grow 30% faster, and snow halves their growth.
World map fields belong to the world: a field harvested in one save is harvested in all of them.
Farm hands and keen gardeners among the townsfolk water plots too, but only you can harvest what you planted.
A honey harvest always leaves 30% for the bees.
Pigs produce nothing while alive. Dogs, cats and horses are kept for company, lifting the party's spirits once a day each.
Building on land you do not own works, but half the value of everything you placed is filed as one bounty.
The later your world's starting year, the better the loot, peaking in 2012.
A level 1 party in a level 60 country finds that country's crates, but not its legends.
A quarter of all item chests hold a keepsake, and about one rare chest in a hundred holds an Expression Seed.
Some world map chests are already open when you find them: somebody got there first.
Twelve strange star types, a pentagram star, a crude oil star and a candle star among them, shine only over patrons' home planets.
Most Omega Tower floors are worlds of their own. Mixed worlds are the commonest kind, and worlds of pure mimics the rarest.
A crash wakes every passenger and keeps them up for an hour.
The camper burns the least fuel at about 80 km/h.
A black hole cannot refuel the starship, but it fills the Schrodingerite store that powers bridge jumps.
Rare Varlenia turns up in about 1.2% of mining time, which is why anyone burns fuel mining asteroids.
Alien traders pay well for Earth goods, and planets with life on them pay for pizza in crafting materials.
The Ouroboros Memory Loop is a hyperdeck part with unlimited memory.
Reading a web page for eight seconds earns 1 to 3 KP, once per page per save.
In Chaos chess, Black's extra pieces move like kings, so losing one never loses the game. The Cheat Meter buys three illegal moves.
In the card duel, two monsters that win the same number of stats destroy each other.
A cabinet always runs the same game, but every world stocks its arcades differently.
A research discovery counts for every save of the world, but only the first party to make it gets the one time rewards.
Bubba can save the world with the power of love.
